title: Foods to Limit or Cook Thoroughly During Pregnancy
excerpt: Food-safety guidance inspired by CDC/NHS/FDA themes: deli meats, unpasteurized dairy, high-mercury fish, and undercooked foods
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, it's essential to choose safe and healthy foods. Pregnant women should limit or cook thoroughly certain foods to avoid the risk of bacterial contamination and ensure the health of both mother and baby. In this article, we will provide information on the types of foods that pregnant women should limit or cook thoroughly.

## Foods to Limit
According to the CDC, NHS, and FDA, pregnant women should limit the following foods:
- Deli meats and hot dogs: These foods have a high risk of Listeria contamination. Pregnant women should avoid eating deli meats and hot dogs unless they are cooked thoroughly.
- Unpasteurized dairy products: Unpasteurized dairy products can contain bacteria like E. coli, Salmonella, and Listeria. Pregnant women should choose pasteurized dairy products or yogurt to ensure safety.
- High-mercury fish: High-mercury fish like shark, swordfish, and king mackerel can harm fetal development. Pregnant women should limit their consumption of these fish and choose low-mercury fish like salmon, sardines, and anchovies.
- Undercooked foods: Undercooked foods like sushi, sashimi, and salad can contain bacteria like Salmonella and E. coli. Pregnant women should avoid eating undercooked foods unless they are cooked thoroughly.

## Foods to Cook Thoroughly
Pregnant women should also cook the following foods thoroughly:
- Meat and poultry: Meat and poultry should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to ensure safety.
- Eggs: Eggs should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to ensure safety.
- Vegetables: Vegetables should be washed and cooked thoroughly to ensure safety.

## Practical Tips
Here are some practical tips to help pregnant women choose safe foods:
- Read food labels: Pregnant women should read food labels to know the ingredients and ensure that the foods are produced and stored safely.
- Choose fresh foods: Pregnant women should choose fresh foods and avoid foods that are past their expiration date or spoiled.
- Cook foods thoroughly: Pregnant women should cook foods thoroughly to ensure safety.

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about food safety, they should seek help from their healthcare provider or a registered dietitian. They can provide information and guidance to help pregnant women choose safe and healthy foods.

## Conclusion
Choosing safe and healthy foods is crucial for pregnant women. By limiting or cooking thoroughly foods that have a high risk of bacterial contamination, pregnant women can ensure the health of both mother and baby. Remember to read food labels, choose fresh foods, and cook foods thoroughly to ensure safety.

## FAQs
Here are some frequently asked questions about food safety during pregnancy:
- Q: Why should pregnant women limit deli meats and hot dogs?
A: Deli meats and hot dogs have a high risk of Listeria contamination, which can harm fetal development.
- Q: How can pregnant women choose safe foods?
A: Pregnant women should read food labels, choose fresh foods, and cook foods thoroughly to ensure safety.
- Q: Can pregnant women eat undercooked foods?
A: No, undercooked foods can contain bacteria like Salmonella and E. coli, which can harm fetal development.
